data.title: Task 1
data.description: How many of the `nmap` top 1000 TCP ports are open on the remote host?
data.hint: Run a `nmap` scan on the target. If you don't specify which ports to scan, it does the top 1000 by default. You can explicitly tell `nmap` to scan the top X ports with the `--top-ports X` option.

data.title: Task 2
data.description: What version of VSFTPd is running on Lame?

data.title: Task 3
data.description: There is a famous backdoor in VSFTPd version 2.3.4, and a Metasploit module to exploit it. Does that exploit work here?
data.hint: Run `msfconole`, searching for vsftpd, and try the exploit. If you need help, check out the free Academy modeule, [Using the Metasploit Framework](https://academy.hackthebox.com/module/details/39).

data.title: Task 4
data.description: What version of Samba is running on Lame? Give the numbers up to but not including "-Debian".

data.title: Task 5
data.description: What 2007 CVE allows for remote code execution in this version of Samba via shell metacharacters involving the `SamrChangePassword` function when the "username map script" option is enabled in `smb.conf`?
data.hint: There are several 2007 CVEs in this version of the software. Make sure you read about them and find the correct one.

data.title: Task 6
data.description: Exploiting CVE-2007-2447 returns a shell as which user?
data.hint: Run the exploit via Metasploit or one of the many proof of concept scripts available on GitHub.

data.title: Submit User Flag
data.description: Submit the flag located in the makis user's home directory.

data.title: Submit Root Flag
data.description: Submit the flag located in root's home directory.

data.title: Task 9
data.description: We'll explore a bit beyond just getting a root shell on the box. While the official writeup doesn't cover this, you can look at [0xdf's write-up](https://0xdf.gitlab.io/2020/04/07/htb-lame.html#beyond-root---vsftpd) for more details. With a root shell, we can look at why the VSFTPd exploit failed. Our initial `nmap` scan showed four open TCP ports. Running `netstat -tnlp` shows many more ports listening, including ones on 0.0.0.0 and the boxes external IP, so they should be accessible. What must be blocking connection to these ports?
data.hint: `iptables` is an example of one of these.

data.title: Task 10
data.description: When the VSFTPd backdoor is trigger, what port starts listening?
data.hint: Read about the exploit. For example, look at [this POC](https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/49757). What does it connect to after triggering the backdoor?

data.title: Task 11
data.description: When the VSFTPd backdoor is triggered, does port 6200 start listening on Lame?
